verdict.rationale: Foreloop documents team-authored 'skills' that encode recurring corrections. Task contracts carry the relevant skills into each run, so agents start with the team's expectations, which is a first-party way to feed conventions to agents. The docs do not say a skill is a context file, how it is authored or stored, or whether it shapes plan and task proposals as well as code execution. missing for 10: explicit context-file format and location, documentation that conventions influence plan/task generation, examples of codebase-convention content, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can add a context file describing my codebase conventions so agents generate more relevant plans and code

citations.quote: Each task contract carries the relevant skills into the run, so an agent starts with your team's expectations rather than being corrected afterwards.
Write a skill when you notice yourself giving an agent the same correction twice.
